info.desc: The Idiot is the debut solo album by American rock singer Iggy Pop. It was the first of two LPs released in 1977 which Pop wrote and recorded in collaboration with David Bowie. Although issued after Low, the opening installment of Bowie's so-called "Berlin trilogy", the pair began writing and recording songs for The Idiot in mid-1976, before Bowie started work on his own album. As such, The Idiot has been claimed as heralding the unofficial beginning of Bowie's "Berlin" period, and is a departure from the hard rock of Pop's former band the Stooges, being compared particularly to Low .

podcast.body: An album from 1977 for which David Bowie co-wrote the song "China Girl." Bowie later covered "China Girl" on his "Let's Dance" album, with the intention of providing significant royalties to Iggy Pop, whose finances were "shaky" in the early 80s. "For the track that became the album's second single, Bowie brought him a song he'd co-written for Iggy Pop's 1977 LP, The Idiot, The aforementioned China Girl."

podcast.body: Iggy Pop's first solo album, work on which began in June 1976 with David Bowie, and was ready by March 1977. Bowie played all instruments except Iggy's vocals. It performed "all right sales-wise," surpassing all Stooges releases, partially due to the Bowie connection. In 1994, Trent Reznor sampled its opening beats from "Nightclubbing" to create a new sound. "The Idiot did all right sales-wise. Certainly way better than anything the stooges had ever released."

podcast.body: Recorded in June at Château d'Hérouville, this was Iggy Pop's first solo album, produced entirely by David Bowie. After its recording, Iggy Pop and Bowie shared a modest flat in Berlin. "En junio entran para grabar el que sería el primer disco como solista de Hip-hop, de Idiot. El álbum está integramente producido por Bowie."

podcast.body: Released in 1977, this album marked a significant step in Iggy Pop's solo career after his struggles with addiction and the initial breakup of The Stooges. It was part of a period where he and David Bowie moved to Berlin and cleaned up their lives, effectively restarting their careers. "Iggy's solo career really got moving with two albums, the Idiot and Lust for Life, both released in 1977."

podcast.body: This album was Ian Curtis's favorite and was put on his stereo by Ian just before he died by suicide on the morning of May 18, 1980. The album played as Ian hanged himself. "Ian went over to the stereo, put on his favorite album, which was The Idiot by Iggy Pop, went up to the garden, got himself a length of rope from the clothesline, and as the sun came up and Iggy sang, Ian hanged himself."

podcast.body: This album, a "grandísimo disco," was recorded in Berlin during the same period as David Bowie's "Berlin Trilogy" and marked the launch of Iggy Pop's successful solo career. Iggy Pop had moved to West Berlin with Bowie, seeking to detoxify from drugs, though he only managed to reduce his consumption and never fully detoxed. "el mismísimo Yipop también trae grabó de idiota en Berlin justo al mismo tiempo, ese grandísimo disco de Yipop con el quina pura su carrera en solitario, justo se grabó en plena, trilogía de Berlin de David Bowie."

podcast.body: This album, along with "Lust for Life," significantly influenced Josh Homme's musical tastes and aspirations after Kyuss disbanded, leading him to explore different styles of music. "It was around this time that Josh discovered albums like Lust for Life and the Idiot. That was the kind of music he wanted to make now."
